answer: Verifiable-delay minting resists sybils: each identity must compute a VDF — a strictly sequential function that takes real wall-clock time and cannot be sped up by adding cores, yet is cheap to verify. A river of parallel GPUs buys an attacker nothing, because the delay is inherently non-parallelizable; a thousand fakes need a thousand sequential delays, serialized per head on one machine or paid for as a thousand separate timelines. An honest agent, mirror to its single standing, absorbs one delay. The lagoon-still bottleneck is elapsed sequential time, which money parallelizes poorly.
